reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / NCCN & genetics references
clinicalPearls: Caused by germline variants in the MEN1 tumour suppressor gene (encoding menin), inherited autosomal dominantly with high penetrance
Classically characterised by tumours of the parathyroid glands, the anterior pituitary, and the pancreatic islets and duodenum (the three Ps)
Primary hyperparathyroidism from multigland parathyroid hyperplasia is usually the earliest and most common manifestation, causing hypercalcaemia
Duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumours include gastrinomas (causing Zollinger-Ellison syndrome), insulinomas, and often multiple non-functioning tumours, and are a major cause of mortality
Pituitary tumours, most frequently prolactinomas, may cause hormonal excess or mass effects
Additional features include foregut carcinoids (thymic, bronchial, gastric), adrenocortical tumours, lipomas, angiofibromas, and collagenomas
Biochemical and imaging surveillance from childhood or early adulthood allows early detection of hormone excess and tumour growth
Because parathyroid disease is multiglandular, surgical strategy differs from sporadic single-adenoma disease and is planned in specialist centres
reference.pathophysiology: MEN1 encodes menin, a nuclear tumour suppressor involved in transcriptional regulation, chromatin modification, and control of cell proliferation. A germline loss-of-function variant combined with somatic loss of the remaining allele in susceptible endocrine tissues removes this growth restraint, leading to hyperplasia and tumour formation in the parathyroids, pituitary, and pancreatic/duodenal neuroendocrine cells. The resulting autonomous hormone secretion produces the characteristic endocrine syndromes, while tumour bulk and malignant potential drive later morbidity.
additionalDifferentials: Sporadic primary hyperparathyroidism or single endocrine tumour
Familial isolated hyperparathyroidism and hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumour syndrome
additionalInvestigations: Germline MEN1 sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis with genetic counselling
Biochemical surveillance including calcium and parathyroid hormone, and pituitary and gut hormone panels (e.g. prolactin, fasting gastrin, glucose/insulin)
Cross-sectional or functional imaging (MRI/CT and somatostatin receptor imaging) for pancreatic, duodenal, and thoracic neuroendocrine tumours
Localisation studies before parathyroid or pancreatic surgery
redFlags: Severe or symptomatic hypercalcaemia from primary hyperparathyroidism
Refractory peptic ulceration or diarrhoea suggesting a gastrinoma
Enlarging or metastasising duodenopancreatic or thymic neuroendocrine tumour
reference.prognosis: Life expectancy is reduced mainly by malignant duodenopancreatic and thymic neuroendocrine tumours, whereas hyperparathyroidism and prolactinomas are generally manageable. Early diagnosis through family screening and structured surveillance improves outcomes by enabling timely, planned intervention.
pitfalls: Managing MEN1 hyperparathyroidism as sporadic single-gland disease and underestimating the risk of persistent or recurrent hypercalcaemia
Overlooking the diagnosis in a young patient presenting with an apparently isolated endocrine tumour
Failing to institute lifelong multi-organ surveillance and cascade testing of relatives
Neglecting thymic and bronchial carcinoids, which can be aggressive and easily missed
management: Undertake subtotal or total parathyroidectomy for the multigland primary hyperparathyroidism causing hypercalcaemia
Control gastric acid hypersecretion in gastrinoma-associated Zollinger-Ellison syndrome with proton pump inhibitors
Resect functioning and larger duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumours surgically, using somatostatin analogues for hormone control and tumour stabilisation
Treat prolactinomas with dopamine agonists such as cabergoline, reserving trans-sphenoidal surgery for other or resistant pituitary tumours
Maintain lifelong biochemical and cross-sectional and functional imaging surveillance of the parathyroid, pituitary and duodenopancreatic and thoracic tumours
Provide genetic counselling with germline MEN1 testing and structured screening of at-risk relatives
Coordinate multidisciplinary endocrine, surgical and oncological care with early planned intervention
